title: Daily Intel Brief, Fri 27 Nov 2026 SGT
body:
Daily Intel Brief, Fri 27 Nov 2026 SGT

A violent Wednesday reversal on Wall Street fed a broad Asian bounce, but oil is firmer, gold is rebounding and bitcoin is still pinned near $60,000. Russia is signalling a fresh energy-grid strike while the US export-control squeeze on chip routing through Southeast Asia keeps widening.

## Top 5 headlines

**Asian equities rebounded on Thursday: the Nikkei closed up about 1.6%, the Kospi about 1.3% and the Hang Seng about 2%, after Wall Street recovered from deep lows.** Even so, Japan is down about 8% for November, Korea about 16% and Taiwan about 15%, so this is a bounce inside a drawdown rather than a regime change. Index closes differ across outlets, so treat the exact percentages as approximate. — [ABC News](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-26/asx-markets-business-news-live-updates-thursday-26-november/107428134), [Coin Edition](https://coinedition.com/asia-market-recap-tariff-relief-and-a-chip-rebound-lift-hang-seng-taiex-and-kospi/)

**The Bank of Korea raised its benchmark rate a quarter point to 3.25% on a 5-2 vote and lifted its 2027 growth forecast to 4.1%.** A hike while Korean equities are down about 16% on the month tightens financial conditions in the market most levered to the AI trade. Reported so far by one live blog, so confirm against the BoK statement. — [ABC News](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-26/asx-markets-business-news-live-updates-thursday-26-november/107428134)

**Reportedly, Nvidia has told partners to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia while it works out compliance with new US export controls.** This is so far an unverified Financial Times report relayed by one live blog, but it lands on the same week the US added Singapore-based firms to its Entity List. If confirmed it hits the Southeast Asian data-centre build-out directly, so watch for a company or Commerce Department statement. — [ABC News](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-26/asx-markets-business-news-live-updates-thursday-26-november/107428134)

**Bitcoin is holding about $60,460 on the Crypto.com BTC perpetual at 23:53 UTC, with the ETH perpetual at about $1,686.** The 24-hour range on BTC was roughly $59,840 to $61,570, a tight band on a US holiday that thinned liquidity. Wall Street reopens for a half session today, so the $60,000 round number is the level to watch for a liquidity-driven break. — Crypto.com price tool

**Oil is firmer: Brent about $95 and WTI about $84 on Thursday afternoon in Australia, with gold at about $3,598 after dipping below $3,500 on Wednesday for the first time since September 2025.** Sources conflict on Brent, since earlier coverage had it near $88 to $90, so the level matters less than the direction. Another tanker reportedly hit a mine in Hormuz and Iran struck Gulf sites after a lull, which keeps the supply-risk premium alive while the 10-year Treasury sits near 4.8%. — [ABC News](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-26/asx-markets-business-news-live-updates-thursday-26-november/107428134), [Al Jazeera](https://aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/11/25/iran-war-live-houthis-threaten-saudi-ports-over-coalitions-hodeidah-order)

## Geopolitics and Security

**Zelensky said Russia is preparing a new mass attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, while Ukraine's General Staff said it struck a Russian oil station in Bashkortostan and an airfield in Volgograd Oblast.** Continued refinery strikes keep Russian product supply tight even with soft crude, and a grid attack raises European gas and power risk into winter. Update: Trump also said he wants Putin to pull back military aggression across Europe, with no concrete talks date reported. — [Kyiv Independent](https://kyivindependent.com/)

## Asia

**Australia's ASX 200 closed up 0.8% at 8,763, led by materials up 3.9% and energy up 3.1%, as the regional rally followed Wall Street's recovery.** Commodity-linked names are the clean expression of the oil and gold rebound, while chips stay the volatile leg. — [ABC News](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-26/asx-markets-business-news-live-updates-thursday-26-november/107428134)

## Singapore

**The Straits Times Index was reported near 4,974, up about 0.9% in one Thursday recap, with outlets disagreeing on the exact close.** The local market is trading against the backdrop of the Section 301 list naming Singapore and the Nvidia shipment report, so export-control headlines are the swing factor. — [Journal Arta](https://journalarta.com/en/2026/11/26/asia-markets-today-nikkei-drops-while-asx-200-gains-ahead-of-jakarta-open/)

## Politics and Elections

**Reuters, as cited by Coin Edition, reports the proposed US tariffs on 14 partners will not stack on top of rates set in July and are unlikely to take effect before February or March.** That timing explains why Asian markets treated the plan as less damaging than feared, and it pushes the real tariff test into early 2027. — [Coin Edition](https://coinedition.com/asia-market-recap-tariff-relief-and-a-chip-rebound-lift-hang-seng-taiex-and-kospi/)

Next 48h: Fri 27 Nov US markets reopen for a half-day session after Thanksgiving, so liquidity stays thin; Section 301 hearings were reportedly set to begin 25 Jan 2027.

Content angle: Thin holiday liquidity can print a crash and a recovery in a day, which tells you more about who is trading than about what anything is worth. Price moves on empty order books are weather, and flows are climate.
"A half-empty market can fake a panic and fake a recovery. Before you trust a move, ask who was actually on the other side of it."
